title: D. Cyclic MEX
statement:
For an array a, define its cost as ∑_{i=1}^n mex ^dagger ([a_1,a_2,…,a_i]).

You are given a permutation^ddagger p of the set {0,1,2,…,n-1}. Find the maximum cost across all cyclic shifts of p.

^daggermex([b_1,b_2,…,b_m]) is the smallest non-negative integer x such that x does not occur among b_1,b_2,…,b_m.

^ddaggerA permutation of the set {0,1,2,...,n-1} is an array consisting of n distinct integers from 0 to n-1 in arbitrary order. For example, [1,2,0,4,3] is a permutation, but [0,1,1] is not a permutation (1 appears twice in the array), and [0,2,3] is also not a permutation (n=3 but there is 3 in the array).

Each test consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^5) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^6) — the length of the permutation p.

The second line of each test case contain n distinct integers p_1, p_2, …, p_n (0 ≤ p_i < n) — the elements of the permutation p.

It is guaranteed that sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 10^6.

For each test case, output a single integer — the maximum cost across all cyclic shifts of p.

In the first test case, the cyclic shift that yields the maximum cost is [2,1,0,5,4,3] with cost 0+0+3+3+3+6=15.

In the second test case, the cyclic shift that yields the maximum cost is [0,2,1] with cost 1+1+3=5.

Input:
```
465 4 3 2 1 032 1 082 3 6 7 0 1 4 510
```

Output:
```
15
5
31
1
```
